title: NY State Senate · District 26
area: Western/southern Brooklyn, including Bay Ridge, Sunset Park, Dyker Heights, Bensonhurst, Gravesend, and parts of Park Slope and Cobble Hill.

context.text: Incumbent Andrew Gounardes (D, Working Families Party) and Tom Stanten (R, Conservative Party) advanced without primary opposition; the Democratic, Republican, Working Families, and Conservative primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were all canceled.

candidates.name: Andrew Gounardes
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 26 (since 2023); previously District 22 (2019-2022)

summary.text: Andrew Gounardes is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent seeking re-election to NY Senate District 26. First elected to the Senate in 2018 (District 22) and representing District 26 since redistricting in 2023, he chairs the Senate Budget and Revenue Committee and has sponsored legislation on AI safety, social media regulation for minors, tax credits for families, and immigration protections.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in political science from Hunter College (2006) and a J.D. from George Washington University Law School (2010).

Worked as an attorney, as counsel to the Brooklyn Borough President, as director of external affairs for the Citizens Committee for New York City, and as a staff assistant in the U.S. Senate before entering elected office.
Defeated incumbent Republican Martin Golden in 2018 to first win a State Senate seat (District 22), after previously losing to Golden in 2012.
Chairs the Senate Budget and Revenue Committee in the 2025-2026 session; also sits on the Judiciary, Codes, Finance, Higher Education, and Insurance committees.

priorities.text: Expand the family safety net through a Working Families Tax Credit providing families up to $1,600 per child, and exempt school supplies from sales tax.
Pursue universal, free child care and expanded afterschool program access statewide.
Create more affordable housing, including via the Faith-Based Affordable Housing Act enabling houses of worship to build affordable housing.
Protect kids online by requiring platforms to turn off open chat and public profiles by default for users under 18.
Advance "New York for All" legislation to limit local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

positions.summary: Has publicly urged the state to implement congestion pricing in Manhattan, citing funding for transit accessibility projects.
Lists universal, free child care and expanded afterschool access as a top legislative priority.

Introduced legislation decoupling New York's tax code from 2025 federal tax law changes, including a corporate expensing rollback and a phaseout of an expanded child-care tax credit for households earning over $500,000 ($1 million joint).
positions.quote: Trump took a hatchet to the federal tax code, carving out big benefits for his billionaire buddies while chopping up funds for crucial programs like Medicaid and food stamps.

positions.summary: Sponsored the New York for All Act (S2235A), which would bar state and local agencies from using resources for civil immigration enforcement or sharing sensitive information with ICE without a judicial warrant; related restrictions on ICE cooperation passed as part of the FY2027 budget in May 2026.

Sponsored a bill requiring the state Department of Environmental Conservation to account for its own permitting role in last-mile trucking pollution in disadvantaged communities, part of a broader climate and transit-investment agenda.
positions.quote: an honest accounting of what's happening on the ground, and that includes the role our own government has played

positions.summary: Priorities include the Faith-Based Affordable Housing Act, which would allow houses of worship to build affordable housing on their property.

record.text: Sponsored the Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act (S6953B), requiring frontier AI developers to implement safety protocols, report critical incidents within 72 hours, and undergo third-party risk evaluation; signed into law December 19, 2025.
Sponsored a bill (S4505) requiring social media platforms with addictive design features to display Surgeon General mental-health warning labels to users under 18; signed into law December 20, 2025.

Sponsored S.410, restricting judges' ability to reduce jury damage awards in workplace discrimination cases except in exceptional circumstances of prejudice or corruption; passed the Senate by June 12, 2025.

Sponsored S7738A, requiring the state to study its own permitting role in last-mile trucking air pollution in disadvantaged communities under the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act; passed the Senate.

Sponsored the New York for All Act (S2235A) limiting state/local cooperation with ICE; related provisions (barring local jails from holding people for ICE, banning new 287(g) agreements, restricting ICE at sensitive locations without a warrant) passed as part of the FY2027 state budget.
Chairs the Senate Budget and Revenue Committee in the 2025-2026 legislative session.

Introduced legislation in December 2025 decoupling New York's tax code from 2025 federal changes, including reversing an immediate-expensing benefit for corporations (projected to raise about $3 billion in 2026) and phasing out an expanded child/dependent care credit for high earners.

summary.text: Tom Stanten is the Republican and Conservative Party candidate challenging incumbent Andrew Gounardes. A retired NYPD Detective Investigator and U.S. Navy veteran, he is running on a public-safety-focused platform and has not previously held elected office.

background.text: Retired NYPD Detective Investigator with more than 20 years in uniform.
U.S. Navy veteran; deployed aboard the USS Carl Vinson.
Small business owner of a motorcycle shop in Sunset Park, Brooklyn.

priorities.text: Fully fund law enforcement, stand with crime victims, and restore public safety on Brooklyn's streets and in the subways.
priorities.quote: fully funding law enforcement, standing with victims, and restoring public safety

priorities.text: Protect gifted and talented programs in schools and give parents "a real voice."
priorities.quote: protect gifted and talented programs in our schools and give parents a real voice

priorities.text: Improve transit reliability, including upgrading sensors on the R train and reducing wait times between trains.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for fully funding law enforcement and restoring public safety across the district.
positions.quote: fully funding law enforcement, standing with victims, and restoring public safety
